II.|TO THE ROMANES.|385}}</noinclude>Apostles, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 28.''}}to preach to al nations. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Apostles vvriting, and preaching, whether more necessarie, and how.}}The writing of the bookes of the Testament, is an other part of Gods prouidence, necessary for the Church in general, but not necessarie for euery man in particular: as to be taught and preached vnto, is for euery one of age and vnderstanding. And therfore S. Peter (vvho was the cheefe of the Commission) wrote litle: many of them wrote nothing at al: and S. Paul that wrote most, vvrote but litle in comparison of his preaching: nor to any but such as were conuerted to the faith by preaching before.

''17. Liueth by faith.''] In the 10. to the Hebrewes, he sheweth by this place of the Prophete ''(Abacuc 2'') that the iust though he liue here in peregrination, and seeth not presently nor enioyeth the life euerlasting promised to him, yet holdeth fast the hope thereof by faith. In this place he applieth the Prophetes wordes further to this sense, That it is our faith, that is to say, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Catholike or Christian faith with good workes iustifieth. & without this faith, no workes whatsoeuer.}}''the Catholike beleefe'' (saith S. Augustine ''li. 3 cont. 2 ep. Pelag''.) ''which maketh a iust man, and distinguisheth betwene the iust and vniust'', and that by the law of faith, and not by the lavv of workes. Whereof it riseth, that the Iew, the Heathen Philosopher, and the Heretike, though they excelled in al vvorkes of moral vertues, could not yet be iust: and a Catholike Christian man liuing but an ordinarie honest life, either not sinning greatly, or supplying his faults by penance, is iust. And this difference riseth by faith. not that faith can saue any man without vvorkes, ''For it is not a reprobate faith that we speake of'', (as the holy Doctor saith) ''but that vvhich worketh by charitie'', and therfore remitteth sinnes and maketh one iust. See S. Augustines place.

''18. Is reuealed.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Not only faith.}}By al the passage folowing you may see, that the Gospel and Christs law consisteth not only in preaching faith, (though that be the ground, and is first alwaies to be done:) but to teach vertuous life and good vvorkes, and to denounce damnation to al them that commit deadly sinnes and repent not. And againe we see that not only lacke of faith is a sinne, but al other actes done against Gods commaundements.

''24. Hath deliuered them vp.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=God is not the author of sin.}}As he saith here, God deliuered them up, so to the Ephesians (c. 4, 19.) he saith of the same persons and things, They deliuered themselves up to all vncleannesse. So that it is not meant here that God doth driue, force, or cause any man to sinne, as diuers blasphemous Heretics do hold: but only that by his just iudgement, for their owne deseruing, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=God punisheth sin by permitting men to fall further and further.}}and for due punishment of their former grievous offences, he vvithholdeth his grace from them, and so suffereth them to fall further into other sins. As, for their crime of Idolatrie, to suffer them to fall into vnnatural abominations: as now for heresie, he taketh his grace and mercie from many, and so they fall headlong into all kind of turpitude, as contrarywise, for ill life, he suffereth many to fall into heresie. And for Christs sake let euery one that is entangled with the Idolatrie of this time, that is to say, vvith these nevv sects, looke vvel into his owne conscience, whether his forsaking the true God, may not come vnto him for a punishment of his former or present ill life which he liueth.

''32. Worthy of death.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Sinnes mortal and venial.}}Here you see vvhy the Church taketh some sinnes to be deadly, and calleth them mortal: to vvit, because al that doe them, are worthie of damnation: others be venial, that is to say, pardonable of their owne nature and not worthy of damnation.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. II.}}}}}}

{{c|''Now also he sheweth that neither the Iewes could be saued by the knovvledge of the Law, of the vvhich they did so much bragge against the Gentils, seing they did notvvithstanding sinne as the Gentils did. 14 And therfore that the true Iew is the Christian (though he be a Gentil) vvho by grace in his hart doeth the good workes that the Lavv commaundeth.''}} {{dropinitial|F|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial F, a hooded figure.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=2|verse=1}}}}OR the vvhich cause thou art inexcusable ô man vvhosoeuer {{sup|‖}} thou be that iudgest. For vvherein thou iudgest an other, thou condemnest thy self. for thou doest the same things vvhich thou iudgest. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=2}}† For vve knovv that the iudgement of God is according to veritie vpon them that doe such things. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=3}}† And doest thou suppose this ô man that iudgest them which doe such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the iudgement of God? {{verse|chapter=2|verse=4}}† Or {{sup|‖}} doest<noinclude>{{rh||Ccc|thou}}</noinclude>
